findings.text: non-blocking: _other_project_plan_finding returns '' for a whole-plan cross-project wait because it requires parsed.stage, so a dispatch waiting on a malformed plan without a '#section' anchor is still held awaiting-upstream by _dispatch_nonrun_wait_state (readiness.py:1147-1150, empty state -> PENDING) but carries no finding naming the plan and its validation error; the three tests cover only the section-anchored form (WAIT_REF 'upstream:upstream-plan#s1').

item_verdicts.diff: read the single commit 57356aca95 against 9ed4c9ee2 file by file: readiness.py adds plan_state_or_error/_other_project_plan_finding/preview_wait_phase and a state_of helper, wait_refs.py wraps two strict reads, dispatch_batch.py adds _wait_verdict/_record_wait_findings and dry-run would_phase/wait_holds reporting; all coherent with the goal.
item_verdicts.done_when: recounted the three cases in tests/test_an_unreadable_upstream_plan_holds_only_its_waiters.py against the done_when: hold-only-the-waiter, dry-run parity and release-after-repair, each with a recorded arm log carrying revision, literal command and closing EXIT=.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is that a malformed plan in one project does not refuse dispatches in another; the diff narrows strict reads to the dispatch's own project (readiness.py:1095-1104, wait_refs.py:385-395) and the test proves the sibling still queues.
item_verdicts.manifest: the source manifest records complete with the three-case gate, both suite arms (58->61 passed, 0 failures), the base-arm negative control (3 failed EXIT=1) and its retry_failures correctly attributed to scaffolding, all consistent with the logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's four declared write paths; every path in git show --stat 57356aca95 is inside them, and the declared optional fragment/figure were not written.

justifications.durability: the three cases fail at the base revision on the validation error (negative-control-base-arm.log, 3 failed EXIT=1), so the tests guard the defect; the dry-run parity arm's wait_holds check compares two code outputs, backstopped by the absolute would_phase literals at tests/test_an_unreadable_upstream_plan_holds_only_its_waiters.py:262-263.
justifications.evidence: baseline_suite-1795380192699466708.log reads '58 passed' EXIT=0 at 9ed4c9ee2; after_suite-1795380267477654875.log reads '61 passed' EXIT=0 at 57356aca95; negative-control-base-arm.log reads '3 failed' EXIT=1 at the base, matching the done_when's gate and its negative control.
justifications.fit: readiness.py:398-412 follows the module's established idiom of broad 'except Exception noqa: BLE001' plan reads (readiness.py:154,203) and names functions by mechanism, introducing no plan or version label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/admission/readiness.py:435-452 and lean admission state_of at readiness.py:1095-1104 scope the strict plan read to the dispatch's own project, so a cross-project malformed plan resolves PENDING; tests/test_an_unreadable_upstream_plan_holds_only_its_waiters.py:222-236 shows the waiting request held with its finding while the sibling queues.
justifications.reuse: preview_wait_phase (readiness.py:454) extends _release.resolve_waits alongside the queue-time writer rather than re-deriving phases, and plan_state_or_error wraps _plan_state_and_text; a search of readiness.py, wait_refs.py, release.py and _schema.py found no pre-existing state-or-error wrapper or wait-phase preview to extend.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 57356aca95 lists only reckon/crew/admission/readiness.py, wait_refs.py, dispatch_batch.py and the new test, every one inside the four declared write paths and nothing else.

review_method: read-only artefact review of the landed commit against its base; no suite re-run
